nodes.label: India DPDP Act 2023 (Digital Personal Data Protection)
Audit-Retention Immutability (H1 Invariant)
nodes.rationale: compliance.delete rows in error_events must survive both erase and delete operations. Three enforcement layers: (1) RLS INSERT policy blocks authenticated users from writing null-user compliance rows; (2) no DELETE/UPDATE for authenticated role; (3) DB CHECK constraint user_id IS NULL when category=compliance.delete. Layer 3 was absent in live DB as of 2026-06 audit. Retaining proof-of-deletion is itself a compliance control under DPDP.

nodes.label: Erase Data vs Delete Account Semantics
nodes.rationale: Erase (erase_account_data RPC) wipes product tables but keeps auth user and anonymizes audit rows. Delete (delete-account edge function) is a two-step flow: erase then auth.admin.deleteUser, removes auth user, cascades product data, retains compliance.delete audit event. Gated by 15-minute reauth window. Two distinct operations with different guarantees that must never be conflated.

nodes.label: Supabase Free-Tier Egress Limits
nodes.rationale: 5 GB/month egress is the first cliff before DB size (500 MB) or CPU. Vercel Hobby has 10s serverless timeout. EAS ~30 builds/month. Middleware already runs getUser() + user_profiles SELECT on every protected request as accepted baseline cost. Egress = bytes × requests is the key metric to optimize.

nodes.label: RLS Tenant Isolation Model
nodes.rationale: All 13 public tables have RLS enabled. rate_limit_counters has RLS with NO policy intentionally (service-role-only, default-deny). 11 RPCs are authenticated-EXECUTE by design. SECURITY DEFINER functions must pin search_path='' to prevent search-path hijack. RLS policies use (select auth.uid()) initplan form for performance.

nodes.label: rate_limit_counters RLS-Enabled No-Policy (Intentional)
nodes.rationale: rate_limit_counters has RLS enabled but no policy — this is intentional (service-role-only, default-deny). Supabase advisor reports rls_enabled_no_policy INFO but this must not be flagged as a missing-policy bug. Do NOT propose adding a policy.

nodes.label: RLS Integration CI Job (mandatory status check)
nodes.rationale: rls-integration is mandatory on every PR with no if: gate because it is the sole automated guard against cross-tenant data leakage. Missing secret causes hard failure not silent skip. Concurrency serialised per ref; cancel-in-progress=false because tests do inline + afterAll cleanup.

nodes.label: Brand Catalog Sync Version Gate
nodes.rationale: sync_default_brand_catalog fires at most once per browser tab per catalog version via CATALOG_SYNC_VERSION constant. Mobile native fix injects AsyncStorage-backed CatalogSyncStorage adapter so marker survives cold boots. Web switches sessionStorage to localStorage so new tabs don't re-sync. Catalog sync is timeout-guarded (6s) to avoid stalling boot.

nodes.label: Password Login Rate Limiting (fail-open)
nodes.rationale: signInWithPasswordAction gated by checkRateLimits with fail-open so missing service-role key cannot lock all users out. Limits: 10/IP/10min, 5/email/15min. Extracted from phoneOtp.ts into shared web/lib/auth/rateLimit.ts. OTP is fail-closed (SMS costs real money). Signup/reset remain client-side and rely on Supabase native limits + Turnstile captcha.

nodes.label: Next.js unstable_cache for Brands (per-user, tag-busted)
nodes.rationale: getServerBrandsWithVariants wrapped in unstable_cache keyed by userId with tag brands:{userId}, revalidate 3600s. Tag invalidation via revalidateTag on brand create/favorite/delete. Cuts Supabase egress on the static-ish brands/variants data (~110 rows per user). Same treatment applicable to get_health_milestones and facts catalog.

nodes.label: PKCE OAuth CSRF Protection
nodes.rationale: Supabase SDK uses PKCE (RFC 7636) instead of classical OAuth state parameter. code_verifier stored in HttpOnly Secure SameSite=Lax cookie; auth server verifies code_verifier matches code_challenge. A stolen code cannot be exchanged from a different browser. Additional defenses: next path allowlist, origin-bound cookie scope, CSP and HSTS. Known caveat: same-browser CSRF theoretically possible if attacker can write to cookie store.

nodes.label: Shared Validation Schema (src/lib/validation.ts)
nodes.rationale: All Zod domain schemas live exclusively in src/lib/validation.ts, the single source of truth. Web accesses via @/* TypeScript path alias resolving to src/*. Repositories always call parseOrThrow before any DB write. Auth-form schemas are kept local to each surface as they have different concerns. Regression test: src/tests/web-schemas-shared.test.ts asserts same module reference.

nodes.label: Cross-Device Auth via Token Hash (verifyOtp)
nodes.rationale: Email links now use token_hash instead of device-bound PKCE code. verifyOtp({token_hash, type}) needs no locally-stored verifier, enabling cross-device link opening. One global template serves web (https) and mobile (smokeledger://) via {{.RedirectTo}}. Mobile custom-scheme links still require app installed on receiving device; Universal Links/App Links deferred.

nodes.label: LinkedIn Launch Post — Smoke Ledger India
Milestone — Streak and Health Progress Markers
Goal — User-Set Reduction or Quit Target
Savings — Potential and Actual INR Savings
AUDIT_PEPPER — Server Secret for Audit Hash Anonymisation
nodes.rationale: A shared server-only secret mixed with user_id before SHA-256 hashing for long-lived audit rows. Allows proving a deletion happened without storing a raw UUID. Non-reversible after auth.users is purged. Rotation severs forensic continuity but strengthens anonymisation — the correct DPDP-best-effort trade-off.

nodes.label: Row-Level Security (RLS) — Per-Row Multi-Tenant Isolation
nodes.rationale: Postgres per-row access control enforced in the database layer, not application code. All 13 public tables have RLS enabled. (SELECT auth.uid()) scalar-subquery form evaluated once as InitPlan for performance on large log sets.

nodes.label: DPDP — India Digital Personal Data Protection Framework
nodes.rationale: Privacy north star: real data export and erasure paths, peppered audit design to prove deletion without re-identifiable data. DPDP-best-effort posture for a pre-launch solo-operated app — not a claim of full formal compliance.

nodes.label: Keyset Pagination — Cursor-Based Log Paging
nodes.rationale: Uses (ts_utc, id) cursor instead of OFFSET/LIMIT to stay fast at any depth and remain stable under concurrent inserts.

nodes.label: 18+ Age Gate — Fail-Closed Adult Verification
nodes.rationale: Age always derived from date of birth, never stored as a stale integer. Fails closed: unparseable or future DOB treated as not-adult. Enforced in DB trigger (handle_new_user) so auth.users INSERT is aborted for minors.

nodes.label: IST Local Date / Local Hour — Timezone-Safe Date Storage
nodes.source_location: glossary: IST / local date / local hour
nodes.rationale: local_date stored as YYYY-MM-DD text to avoid timezone re-interpretation. Requires explicit ::date cast in SQL comparisons. Domain layer uses plain string math (dayShift) to avoid timezone drift.

nodes.label: Domain Layer — Pure TypeScript Functions (src/domain/)
nodes.rationale: Pure TypeScript with no Supabase imports, no async, no side effects. Runs identically on native app, web server, and in Jest. Structural enforcement: nothing in src/domain/ does async work.

nodes.label: Monorepo Shared src/ — Single Source of Truth for Business Logic
nodes.rationale: Both React Native (Expo) and Next.js runtimes share src/ so business logic (cigarette log math) is written once and runs everywhere. @/ alias resolves to src/ on both platforms via tsconfig paths.

nodes.label: Repository Pattern — One File Per DB Table
Zustand Store — In-Memory Session and Auth Cache
RealtimeRefresher — Cross-Device Data Sync via Supabase Realtime
Metro / Hermes CJS Shim — Fixing @supabase/supabase-js ESM Dynamic Import
nodes.rationale: Hermes cannot statically compile dynamic import with non-literal specifier; forces dist/index.cjs for @supabase/supabase-js so CJS require() handles optional OTel gracefully.

nodes.label: Zod Schema Validation — Single Source of Truth for Allowed Values
nodes.rationale: Zod schemas and Postgres CHECK constraints kept in sync intentionally. If a value passes Zod it will pass the matching Postgres CHECK. Repository always calls parseOrThrow before any Supabase call.

nodes.label: Next.js Server Components + unstable_cache — Web Server-Side Data Fetching
v_daily_summary_user — Security-Invoker Aggregation View
nodes.rationale: security_invoker = true so RLS on cigarette_logs applies at query time. Earlier version without security_invoker was a real bug — any authenticated user could read every user's daily aggregates.

nodes.label: smoke_seed Schema — Server-Only Brand Catalog and Facts
nodes.rationale: No RLS but shielded by REVOKE ALL FROM PUBLIC and living outside public schema. PostgREST cannot directly reach these tables.

nodes.label: handle_new_user Trigger — Auth User Creation + 18+ Gate + Brand Seed
Running Mean Price — price_sum_inr / price_count Welford Update
nodes.rationale: Replaces biased midpoint hack. avg_price_inr is a true running mean updated atomically in create_log_with_rate_limit, avoiding race conditions.

nodes.label: Cross-Device Magic Link — token_hash Priority in createSessionFromUrl
nodes.source_location: The three link shapes and createSessionFromUrl
nodes.rationale: token_hash+type is checked first (verifyOtp — works across devices). code (PKCE exchangeCodeForSession) is same-device only. Priority order fixes the cross-device open failure: request on phone, open on laptop now works.

nodes.label: Auth Rate Limiting — Token-Bucket via consume_rate_limit RPC
nodes.rationale: Fail-open: if service-role key is missing or DB unavailable, check passes and Supabase native limits serve as backstop. Known trade-off, not a bug.

nodes.label: Identity Field Immutability — DB Trigger Enforcement for full_name / DOB / gender
nodes.source_location: Immutability of name, date of birth, and gender
nodes.rationale: RLS UPDATE policy is intentionally wide (id = auth.uid()) and cannot express per-column restrictions. The trigger is the only place where set-once semantics can be enforced at DB level.

nodes.label: Mobile Number 30-Day Rate Limit
nodes.rationale: DB trigger owns the window and sets mobile_changed_at server-side; client cannot supply a forged timestamp. Client-side canChangeMobile check is UX-only — DB trigger is the actual enforcement.

nodes.label: create_log_with_rate_limit RPC — Atomic Log Insert with Rate Limiting
nodes.source_location: Creating a log: createLog and the rate-limit RPC
nodes.rationale: SECURITY DEFINER RPC doing idempotency check (client_op_id), 50/hour rate limit, insert, and brand_variants running-mean update atomically in one Postgres transaction.

nodes.label: Brand / Variant Catalog — Per-User Seeded from smoke_seed
Brand Name Snapshot — Denormalised Historical Accuracy on Logs
nodes.rationale: brandNameSnap / variantSnap written at insert time and never updated when brand catalog changes, so historical entries always read correctly even after renames or deletes.

nodes.label: client_op_id — Idempotency Key for Safe Log Retries
nodes.rationale: Partial unique index on (user_id, client_op_id) WHERE NOT NULL. RPC returns existing row on collision rather than inserting duplicate, making log creation safe under flaky mobile networks.

nodes.label: Goals, Insights, and Savings — Smoke Ledger India
generateInsights — Rules-Based Insight Engine
nodes.rationale: Explicit rules engine, never an LLM. Every insight ships with supporting evidence and a confidence level. Deliberate absence of any AI claim is a trust decision.

nodes.label: milestoneProgress — Body Recovery Timeline Since Last Cigarette
Character Companion — Emotional Layer / On-Screen Mascot
Achievement Suppression — Per-Session Cap After 2 Deliberate Dismissals
nodes.source_location: Achievement celebrations are self-limiting per session
nodes.rationale: Auto-dismiss (5.2s timeout) does not count toward cap — only intentional tap/button/back/Escape. Counter lives on useSession, zeroed on logout.

nodes.label: Reduce Motion — Accessibility Gate for Confetti and Animation
Security and Privacy — Smoke Ledger India
SECURITY DEFINER + search_path Hygiene
nodes.rationale: All SECURITY DEFINER functions pin search_path = '' to prevent search-path injection. They run with function-owner privileges; inheriting caller's search_path could allow a creative caller to shadow tables via a schema they control.

nodes.label: Erase Data vs Delete Account — Two Distinct Data Removal Operations
nodes.rationale: Erase wipes product tables and anonymises audit rows but keeps auth identity (user can re-onboard). Delete removes auth identity entirely. Ordering constraint: erase_account_data must run before auth.admin.deleteUser; if erase fails, deletion aborts.

nodes.label: Compliance Delete Tamper-Resistance — 3-Layer error_events Protection
nodes.rationale: Layer 1: RLS INSERT policy blocks authenticated users from inserting compliance.delete rows. Layer 2: No UPDATE/DELETE policy for authenticated — default deny. Layer 3: CHECK constraint forces user_id IS NULL when category = 'compliance.delete'. Authenticated users cannot see, create, or modify these forensic tombstones.

nodes.label: Re-Authentication Gate — 15-Min Window for Account Deletion
nodes.rationale: Blocks a stolen refresh token from being used to delete the account. Attacker would need a recent full authentication, not just a long-lived session token.

nodes.label: ALLOWED_ORIGINS — Edge Function CORS Allowlist
nodes.rationale: Wildcard * only accepted when ENVIRONMENT != production. Non-browser clients (mobile, curl) send no Origin header and are accepted — bearer token is the real gate.

nodes.label: rls-integration CI Job — Mandatory Cross-Tenant Isolation Safety Net
nodes.rationale: Deliberately mandatory — no if: guard, exits 1 if secrets absent. Sole automated cross-tenant data leakage safety net. branch protection must include it as required status check.

nodes.label: EAS Build — Expo Application Services for Android APK/AAB
Supabase Free Tier — Auto-Pause Risk and Limits
nodes.rationale: Most common production availability risk: auto-pauses after one week of zero API calls. No alerting configured.

nodes.label: Smoke Ledger India — Product Specification (Mother Book)
Spec Drift Detection — npm run spec:drift
nodes.rationale: Each spec section declares source globs in spec-manifest.json. After code changes, drift-check.mjs reports sections whose declared sources changed since last_verified_commit. Signal to run /spec-update.

nodes.label: Humanify Voice Rule
nodes.rationale: Write for a human: plain, clear, a little warm. Full sentences over bullets, explain why not just what, no stilted AI cadence. A new engineer should read a section top to bottom and simply understand it.

nodes.label: Living Spec System — Phase 1 Implementation Plan
nodes.author: Trishit (with Claude)

nodes.label: Glob Matcher + Section Mapping Library (glob.mjs / sections.mjs)
Mother Book v1 Generation (10 spec sections)
Spec Manifest JSON (code-to-section map)
nodes.rationale: Single file mapping code globs to spec sections with last_verified_commit. This enables cheap targeted updates — only changed sections are opened. The difference between an update costing 3 sections vs the entire product.

nodes.label: Token Discipline (section-scoped updates)
nodes.rationale: A spec that is expensive to update will rot. Every operation is section-scoped, fan-out per section, never re-reading unchanged context. Cost is bounded to changed sections × changed files.

nodes.label: CI Drift Guard (scripts/spec-drift-check.mjs)
nodes.rationale: Warning-mode pre-launch (exit 0 by default, exit 1 with --strict). A blocking gate that fights rebases would cost more than it's worth pre-launch. Can be promoted post-launch by flipping one flag.

nodes.label: Spec-Driven Development
nodes.rationale: From here on, the spec leads and the code follows. When the truth is scattered, every change starts with re-discovery, onboarding is slow, and it is easy to violate an invariant nobody wrote down.

RLS / Authz Integration Test Layer (Jest, dedicated test Supabase users)
canSeed() Gate (prod-safety skip mechanism)
nodes.source_location: How authenticated E2E stays safe on prod
nodes.rationale: Specs skip entirely when SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY/URL/anon are absent. Nothing runs — and nothing hits prod — on an unconfigured machine or CI without secrets.

nodes.rationale: Character stroke resolves to var(--character-ink, var(--text)). Since --text is already defined in both :root (light) and .dark (dark) scopes of globals.css, the character auto-flips with the existing dark-mode toggle — zero per-component code change required.

nodes.rationale: Global media-query rule in character-animations.css disables every figure animation, all confetti, and the modal rise. Figure stays visible in a neutral resting pose. prefers-reduced-motion is the sole off-switch.
